newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin seeks referendum on burying Lenin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin seeks referendum on burying Lenin.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin suggested on Friday that a referendum be held on whether to remove Bolshevik leader Vladimir Lenin from his Red Square mausoleum and give the corpse a Christian burial, Itar-Tass news agency said.
"Let the people decide whether to bury him in a Christian way or leave things as they are," Tass quoted Yeltsin as saying during a visit to St Petersburg, cradle of the 1917 Bolshevik revolution.

"On the one hand, we know how many troubles he brought to Russia," Yeltsin told a meeting of a presidential council on culture. "On the other, it is our history, and we cannot hide from it." He suggested holding a referendum in the autumn.
Interfax news agency quoted him as saying: "I hope we will gradually rid Red Square of its status of a cemetery."

Lenin's mummified body, shielded behind bullet-proof glass in the polished red marble mausoleum, has become the focus of an intensive struggle between reformers, led by the Kremlin leader, and the communist opposition for whom Lenin is an idol.
The opposition-dominated State Duma, the lower house of parliament, has passed a law banning any changes in the appearance of Red Square, but Yeltsin has not signed the law and is unlikely to do so.
